$comment: Normative test vectors for AAP-ConductRecord/v2 (specs/aap-conductrecord-v2.md §4-§5). fold(h0,[t1..tn]): h_i = SHA-256(h_{i-1} || UTF-8(canonicalJson(t_i))), h as 32 raw bytes, result lowercase hex; fold(h0,[]) = h0. canonicalJson sorts keys recursively and writes no whitespace. Shared by the aip verifier tests, the @mnemom/sdk parity tests, the mnemom-api producer tests and its pgTAP test.

decision_refs.$comment: The id is lowercased before hashing: the third and fourth ids are one id in two cases and give one ref. In SQL the prefix is E'AAP-DecisionRef/v1\n' (or 'AAP-DecisionRef/v1' || chr(10)); a plain '...\n' literal keeps a backslash and an n.

row_normalisation.$comment: Raw stored rows and the §4 tuple each normalises to, as canonical JSON text (null: the row fails the build). Shared by the aip tests (citationFromRow, actFromRow) and the api pgTAP tests (record_ckpt_tuple, record_act_tuple). Postgres regex bounds stop at 255, so SQL writes each bounded pattern as '^[class]+$' AND length(x) BETWEEN 1 AND n.

checkpoints.name: commitment null: unbound, key id dropped
bound, key id fails ID_RE: key id null
checkpoint id 257 characters: the build fails
checkpoint id with a space: the build fails

grouping.$comment: groupActCounts(counts, withheld) (§7) and the expected result. The producer's SQL returns only plain GROUP BY counts; the ranking, the 64-row cap and the order are this one function.

cases.name: under the cap: one row per key, null first, tools by code point
overflow: 44 line-bearing names by count kept, the rest folded into null rows
overflow tie-break: equal counts rank by mode, verdict, then tool name
